PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person
shall make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and may be enacted by one motion. There will be
no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

 City Council  Agenda  November 14, 2023

1.  Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 7A, 7B, and 7C
  The City Council and Successor Agency will consider for approval the bills
  and claims set forth in Warrant Registers No.7A dated November 14, 2023,
  No. 7B dated October 25, 2023, through November 7, 2023, 7C dated
  November 18, 2023 through November 23, 2023.
  Attachments:  7A 2023
  7B 2023
  7C 2023

2.  Approval of Minutes
  The City Council and Successor Agency will consider for approval the minutes
  of the City Council meeting of Tuesday, October 24, 2023, held at 5:00 p.m.
  Attachments:  2023-10-24 CC Minutes

  SCHEDULED MATTERS

3.  Presentation/Update from the Sheriff's Department Regarding Public Safety
  in the City of Commerce
4.  Citadel Black Friday Weekend Sales Event Planning Update
  The City Council will receive and file an update on coordination efforts for the
  Citadel Black Friday Weekend Sales Event
  Attachments:  Staff Report
  Black Friday PP Pres

5.  Slauson Corridor Improvements from I-5 to I-710 Project Concept Plan
  The City Council will consider approving a Slauson Corridor Improvements
  Concept Plan.
  Attachments:  Staff Report
  Slauson PP Pres Options

6.  Classifying Property Located at 5440 Telegraph Road in the City of
  Commerce, California as Surplus Land Pursuant to the Surplus Land Act
  The  Successor  Agency  to  the  Commerce  Community  Development
  Commission will consider for adoption a Resolution declaring real property
  located at 5440 Telegraph Rd. as Surplus Land, in accordance with the
  Surplus Lands Act, and authorizing staff to proceed with the disposition of the
  Land in the City of Commerce, California.
  Attachments:  Staff Report
  Resolution

7.  Classifying Property at 4560 Washington Boulevard in the City of
  Commerce, California as Surplus Land Pursuant to the Surplus Land Act
  The  Successor  Agency  to  the  Commerce  Community  Development
  Commission will consider for adoption a Resolution declaring real property
  located at 4560 Washington Blvd. as Surplus Land, in accordance with the
  Surplus Lands Act, and authorizing staff to proceed with the disposition of the
  Land in the City of Commerce, California.
  Attachments:  Staff Report
  Resolution

  ORDINANCES

8.  Second Reading and Adoption of an Ordinance Amending Municipal Code
  by Adding Chapter 5.18 Mobile Food Vending
  The City Council will consider for adoption and second reading, by title only,
  an Ordinance Amending Commerce Municipal Code, Title 5 "Business
  Regulations and Licensing" by Adding Chapter 5.18 "Mobile Food Vending".
  Attachments:  Staff Report
  Ordinance
  Application

  PUBLIC HEARING

9.  Resolution Adopting Certain Fundings and Approving Energy Services
  Contract for Energy Related Improvements to City Facilities with Alliance
  Building Solutions, Inc. and Associated Financing with Alliance Funding
  Solutions, Inc, in the Form of a Tax-Exempt Lease - Continuance of this
  Item to the Next City Council Meeting
  The City Council will consider continuing this agenda item to the next regular
  scheduled meeting for adopting a Resolution approving certain Funding and
  Approving Energy Services Contract for Energy Related Improvements to City
  Facilities with Alliance Building Solutions, Inc. and associated financing with
  Alliance Funding Solutions, Inc, in the Form of a Tax-Exempt Lease finding
  that all requirements pursuant to Government Code 4217 for the upgrades of
  the City facilities have been met.
CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS

ADJOURNMENT
Written materials distributed to the City Council are available for public inspection immediately
following the posting of this agenda (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council meetings)
in the City Clerk's Office, at Commerce City Hall, 2535 Commerce Way, Commerce, California,
and the Central Library, 5655 Jillson Street, Commerce, California.
Meeting facilities are accessible to persons with disabilities. ln compliance with the Americans
with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, notify
the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 722-4805 at least 24 hours prior to the meeting.
